summary: Short system card for GPT-5.5 Instant, the default fast ChatGPT model. Reports disallowed-content, vision, dynamic mental-health, jailbreak, prompt-injection, HealthBench, hallucination and first-person-fairness evals, plus Preparedness bio/chem and cyber capability evals and safeguard evals. It is the first Instant model treated as High in Biological & Chemical and Cybersecurity.

framework.name: Preparedness Framework
framework.level_or_determination: High capability in Biological and Chemical and in Cybersecurity (treated as); below High in AI Self-Improvement
framework.quote: GPT-5.5 Instant is our first Instant model to be treated as High Capability in the Biological and Chemical domain, as well as in the Cybersecurity domain.

cbrn_bio_chem.finding: Treated as High in bio/chem as a precaution; exceeds median expert on virology MCQ, just over 80% expert consensus on tacit knowledge only if refusals counted as successes, below expert baseline on ProtocolQA and TroubleshootingBench.
cbrn_bio_chem.quote: We are treating this launch as High capability in the Biological and Chemical domain, activating the associated Preparedness safeguards.

cyber.finding: Results closely match GPT-5.4 Thinking (treated as High), so GPT-5.5 Instant is treated as High; evals run at xhigh effort above deployed setting.
cyber.quote: GPT-5.5 Instant closely matches the results for GPT-5.4 Thinking in the cybersecurity evaluations below. Because of this, we similarly treat GPT-5.5 Instant as High under the Preparedness Framework.

autonomy_ai_rnd.finding: AI Self-Improvement evals were not run; model judged below High because it is less capable than GPT-5.5 Thinking.
autonomy_ai_rnd.quote: AI Self-Improvement capability evals were not run, as GPT-5.5 Instant is less capable than GPT-5.5 Thinking across several intelligence evaluations.

harmful_content_refusal.finding: Comparable to GPT-5.3 Instant except statistically significant regressions on gore and sexual content, which are covered by system-level and age-prediction mitigations.
harmful_content_refusal.quote: We find that GPT-5.5 Instant is comparable (i.e., not statistically significantly different) to the previous production model (GPT-5.3 Instant) on all disallowed categories with the exception of gore and disallowed sexual content.

evals: multiturn jailbreak eval derived from internal red-teaming (worst-case defender success rate)
jailbreak_robustness.finding: Results shown only in a figure; a regression from GPT-5.3 Instant is noted and results are framed as directional.
jailbreak_robustness.quote: We are actively iterating on the evaluation structure and view these results, including the regression from GPT-5.3-Instant, as directional rather than definitive.

prompt_injection.quote: GPT-5.5 Instant is comparable to its predecessors on these indicators.

evals: High Stakes (medical/legal/financial) with web-enabled LLM grader
honesty_hallucination.finding: Significant factuality improvements over GPT-5.3 Instant across all prompt sets (figure only).
honesty_hallucination.quote: We find that GPT-5.5 Instant has significant improvements on factuality over GPT-5.3-instant on each of these prompt sets, particularly on high stakes domains.

bias_fairness.finding: Broadly comparable to prior instant models; no statistically meaningful difference.
bias_fairness.quote: GPT-5.5 Instant scored 0.0101 on this metric, broadly comparable to GPT-5.2-instant and GPT-5.3-instant.

child_safety.finding: Reported as one category of the disallowed-content benchmark; age-prediction protections for likely minors described.
child_safety.quote: For users we believe may be under 18, we apply additional age-appropriate content protections that further restrict sexual content and exposure to gore.

evals: Dynamic Mental Health Benchmarks with Adversarial User Simulations (mental health, emotional reliance, self-harm)
self_harm_wellbeing.finding: Largely comparable to GPT-5.3 Instant; emotional reliance regression not significant; online experimentation showed no increase.
self_harm_wellbeing.quote: We find that 5.5-instant is largely comparable on these evaluations to 5.3-instant.

evals: Biological safety evals (production, synthetic easy/hard), model-only and model+monitor
system_safeguards.finding: Model-only bio safety regressed sharply on hard synthetic set; adding automated monitors brings end-to-end performance to 0.923. Safeguards include refusal training, monitors, actor-level enforcement, security controls.
system_safeguards.quote: Given the observed regressions on the synthetic evaluations, we subsequently ran our evaluations across both our model and our automated safety monitors to better understand the end-to-end safeguard stack users will encounter in production.

notable_new_eval_methods: Merged hate+harassment category and renamed violence to gore (p.5)
Bio safeguard evals reported both model-only and model+automated-monitor (p.20)

self_reported_limitations.text: Earlier Standard disallowed-content evals had become relatively saturated, motivating Production Benchmarks.
Jailbreak eval still being iterated; results directional rather than definitive.
Evaluations represent a lower bound for potential capabilities.
CTF, CVE-Bench and Cyber Range each have important limitations; excelling on all three is necessary but not sufficient for High.
Disparities between offline mental-health evals and online testing to be investigated.

notes: No alignment, deception, sycophancy, or third-party evaluation sections. Many results only in figures.
